== Biography ==
{{Ireland Native}}
{{Occupation|image=Wikimedia_Commons_photos-3.jpg|text=was a linen weaver}}

'''Robert Glasgow''' was a linen weaver living at '''Donbought''', also written '''Dunbought''' or '''Doonbought''', in Dunaghy parish, County Antrim. His recorded age of forty in the 1851 census suggests birth about '''1811'''; the return gives County Antrim as his birthplace.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, barony of Kilconway, parish of Dunaghy, Donbought, household 16. [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Donbought/16/ National Archives of Ireland, legacy household locator]. [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf ''1851 Irish Census Returns: comma-delimited transcription''], printed p. 100, household 16, including the death entry for Jane Glasgow. See also {{Ancestry Record|62025|538377}}.</ref>

He married '''Margaret''' in '''1833''', according to the census return. No separate marriage-register entry has yet been established for the couple. Margaret was thirty-seven in 1851 and was also recorded as born in County Antrim.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /> Her proposed maiden name, Dunseath or Dunseeth, is discussed below.

The profile associates this family with Robert and Margaret Glasgow of '''Plainfield, Illinois'''. That remains a working identification, rather than an independently demonstrated link between the Irish and American households. The proposed father, [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]], also remains uncertain.

=== Household in 1851 ===

The return records '''eight living residents''': Robert and Margaret, four daughters and two sons. A fifth daughter, Jane, appears in the separate death section, not among the people alive in the household.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /><ref name="DonboughtScott">W. Scott and W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/census/1851censuskilconway.pdf ''1851 Census for some Parishes and Townlands in the Barony of Kilconway, Co. Antrim''], dated 7 May 2014, printed pp. 77-78, references 7883-7890, Dunbought household 16. This transcription calls the seven-year-old son Samuel; the detailed comma-delimited transcription calls him Daniel.</ref>

'''[[Glasgow-1366|Jane Glasgow]]''', their daughter, had died in '''winter 1847''', aged '''five'''. The detailed transcription records the cause of death as unknown. Her entry accounts for the earlier description of two sons and five daughters, but the household should not be described as having seven children living there in 1851.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" />

=== American records associated with this profile ===

The retained 1880 United States census citation places a Robert Glasgow at '''Plainfield, Will County, Illinois''': enumeration district 210, page 405D, NARA microfilm T9, roll 260. The original household image was not independently examined for this revision.<ref name="Census1880">1880 United States Federal Census, Plainfield, Will County, Illinois; enumeration district 210; p. 405D; NARA microfilm publication T9, roll 260. {{Ancestry Record|6742|47116957}}. Citation retained from the imported profile.</ref>

A published transcription of '''Plainfield Township Cemetery''' records '''Robert Glasgow, died 10 January 1888, aged 75''', described as “Father”. It also records '''Margaret, wife of Robert Glasgow''', born '''12 May 1813''' and died '''16 June 1886'''. These are cemetery-transcription details, not independently inspected civil death records.<ref name="PlainfieldCemetery">Selina Brown, contributor, [https://www.interment.net/data/us/il/will/plainfield/plain_fg.htm ''Plainfield Township Cemetery, Plainfield, Will County, Illinois: surnames F-G''], Interment.net, contributed 15 November 2007; entries for Robert and Margaret Glasgow.</ref>

The Find a Grave memorial attached to the earlier profile is '''113062074'''. The memorial photograph has not been independently inspected for this revision.<ref name="FindAGrave">[https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/113062074/robert-glasgow Find a Grave, memorial 113062074, Robert Glasgow]. See also {{Ancestry Record|60525|67006055}}.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1367]] is assessed at 54% (possible). The elder Robert of Glenleslie fits the father generation of the Donbought weaver born c 1811. His age also fits the 1825 Doonbought tithe occupier far better than the younger man, while a Robert witnesses the elder’s 1851 will. The combined local succession and associate evidence makes this a useful specific father hypothesis, but neither identification nor fatherhood is explicit.

Possible 54%; the Donbought-to-Illinois adult identity and each unnamed Robert bridge remain separate uncertainties.

Next useful test: Identify the will witness and trace the Doonbought holding.

Source basis already held: [http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Dunaghy/Donbought/16/ National Archives of Ireland, legacy household locator]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



=== Proposed father: Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie ===

'''The father-son relationship with [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]] remains uncertain.''' The older man was seventy-two in 1851, married to Catherine, and therefore of a suitable age to be this Robert's father. His household identifies sons John and Samuel, but does not identify the married Robert at Donbought as another son.<ref name="Glenleslie1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy, Glenleslie, household 23. [https://durrushistory.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/10/1851irishcensusreturnscommadelimitedtextfilejul24_071.pdf Detailed comma-delimited transcription], printed p. 103, including sons John and Samuel absent in America.</ref>

The older Robert is the leading known chronological candidate for '''Robert Glasco of Doonbought in the 1825 tithe applotment'''. He would have been about forty-six, compared with about fourteen for this Robert. The tithe entry, however, gives no age, wife, children or connection to Glenleslie. It neither establishes the identity of the older occupier nor demonstrates father-son succession to a particular holding.<ref name="Tithe1825">W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/182030stithe/tithenorthantrimrevisionnamespdf.pdf ''Data from the Tithe Applotment Books covering the Baronies of Cary, Dunluce and Kilconway in North Antrim plus the Barony of N. E. Liberties, Co. Londonderry''], surname order, dated 17 October 2016, printed p. 41, compiler's index 5804: Robert Glasco, Doonbought [Dunbught No. 2], Dunaghy, 1825. The index number is not an original property-lot number. Original tithe-book image not inspected.</ref>

The earlier research transcription of the Glenleslie man's '''3 February 1851 will''' lists a Robert Glasgow among the witnesses, but does not identify him as this man or as a son. The attestation and signature layout require checking before that name is treated as a separately identified witness. The will's reported provision for daughter Margaret and her Young children does not establish this Robert's parentage.<ref name="GlenleslieWill">Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie, will dated 3 February 1851, proved 13 February 1854; National Archives of Ireland copy, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJ8-MQQJ?view=fullText FamilySearch, image 229]. Details retained from the supplied Glenleslie profile's earlier research transcription; the image was not re-examined for this revision.</ref>

The fact that the will summary also omits the independently identified sons John and Samuel means it cannot be treated as an exhaustive list of the older man's children. It neither excludes nor proves this Robert as another son. Catherine's maternity is likewise unproved; an uncertain paternal attachment must not automatically become a confident attachment to both parents.

=== Daniel or Samuel: the disputed census name ===

The two examined transcriptions disagree over the seven-year-old son. The detailed comma-delimited transcription gives '''Daniel Glasgow'''; Scott and Macafee's table gives '''Samuel Glasgow''', reference 7889. These are competing readings of the '''same census entry''', not two sons or two independent records.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /><ref name="DonboughtScott" />

A saved crop of the handwriting in rows 6-8 shows the corresponding sequence of a nine-year-old daughter, the disputed seven-year-old son and Robert aged two. The crop was examined, but it lacks the full page heading and comparison handwriting, and the disputed forename has not been treated as settled.<ref name="CensusCrop">Cropped image of the handwritten census name-and-age columns, rows 6-8, supplied by the profile manager and retained with the research materials. The ages are 9, 7 and 2; the central forename is disputed. The complete original return should accompany this crop when publishing the image.</ref> The current [[Glasgow-1397|Daniel Glasgow]] profile is retained as the navigation link; no additional Samuel child is created from the alternative transcription.

The nine-year-old daughter's name is given as '''Netta''' in the examined transcriptions and as '''Motta''' in the existing tree. The spellings should not be silently treated as separate people.

=== The Ireland-Illinois identification ===

The Illinois identification needs to be demonstrated separately from the proposed Glenleslie parentage. Similar names, approximate ages and the associated family trees are useful starting points, but a tree attachment is not an independent source.

The census age of forty suggests birth about '''1810-1811''', conventionally recorded here as about 1811. The Illinois cemetery age of seventy-five at death in January 1888 suggests birth about '''1812-1813'''. This is a discrepancy to retain, not a reason to manufacture an exact birth date. Cemetery location also does not establish place of death.<ref name="DonboughtDetailed" /><ref name="PlainfieldCemetery" />

No inspected passenger record, naturalisation record or other source establishes an emigration date or shows that the whole household travelled together.

=== Griffith's Valuation ===

The Dunaghy valuation index lists '''Robert Glasgow at Doonbought''', along with '''John Dunseath''' in the same townland. A separate entry lists '''Margaret Glasgow at Glenleslie'''.<ref name="GriffithDunaghy">[https://www.failteromhat.com/griffiths/antrim/dunaghy.php Fáilte Romhat, Griffith's Valuation index, Dunaghy parish, County Antrim], Robert Glasgow and John Dunseath at Doonbought; Margaret Glasgow at Glenleslie. Name-and-townland index, not an inspected original valuation page or map.</ref> A parish transcription gives the valuation coverage as '''1861-1862'''; the date of the individual original Doonbought page has not been independently verified.<ref name="GriffithDate">[https://www.irishgenealogyhub.com/antrim/griffiths-valuation/parish-of-dunaghy.php Irish Genealogy Hub, ''Griffith's Valuation: Dunaghy Parish, County Antrim''], heading giving coverage as 1861 and 1862.</ref>

The indexed Robert is a candidate continuation of the 1851 Donbought householder. His identity, exact plot, acreage, immediate lessor and subsequent revision history remain unverified. The entry should not yet be used to assert that this Robert emigrated after 1862.

=== Margaret's proposed maiden name ===

Margaret is attached in the existing tree under the surname '''Dunseeth''', with '''Dunseath''' appearing in another family-tree lead. An Ancestry tree-derived entry for '''Samuel Glasgow''', reportedly born 8 November 1841 and deceased 19 January 1918 at Plainfield, names his parents as Robert Glasgow and Margaret Dunseath. The underlying death record or obituary has not been inspected.<ref name="SamuelTree">[https://www.ancestry.com/genealogy/records/results?firstName=samuel&amp;lastName=glasgow Ancestry, ''Samuel Glasgow Family History Records''], tree-derived entry naming Robert Glasgow and Margaret Dunseath as parents. This is a research lead, not an inspected original parentage record.</ref>

Before this can establish Margaret's maiden name, that Samuel must be connected to this household. The reported 1841 birth differs from the approximate 1843-1844 birth implied by the seven-year-old son in 1851, and the Irish child's forename is itself disputed. Another FamilySearch family summary dates the Illinois Samuel to 1843, illustrating the variation between online trees rather than resolving it.<ref name="SamuelFamilySearch">[https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/LR1F-NC8/catherine-e.-glasgow-1873-1950 FamilySearch Family Tree, Catherine E. Glasgow (1873-1950), LR1F-NC8], parent summary giving Samuel Glasgow as 1843-1918 and Martha Ann Isdal as her mother. User-contributed tree summary.</ref>

The local Dunseath surname is independently represented by John Dunseath's Doonbought valuation entry and a Clough Cemetery plot-owners' register entry for '''John Dunseath of Dunbought''': original registration '''353''', '''five graves''', notes '''1076, 1077 and 1078'''. The individual plot entry is undated; it does not name five interments or identify John's relationship to Margaret. Its registration number is not a current individual grave number.<ref name="CloughDunseath">Nancy Crocetti and Alistair McCartney, transcribers (2012), Jim McKane, compiler, [https://www.cotyroneireland.com/burial/clough2.html ''Clough Cemetery (aka Dunaghy Old Graveyard) Plot Owners, Clough, Dunaghy Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland c1875-1937''], entry 353, John Dunseath, Dunbought.</ref>

=== The 1876 Kendall County directory ===

The original imported profile mentioned an image from the ''Biographical Directory of the Voters and Tax-Payers of Kendall County, Illinois''. The local index to the '''1876''' volume gives these precise page references:<ref name="KendallIndex">[https://kendallkin.org/databases/948/A%2CG/19.html Kendall County, Illinois Genealogy, ''Index to Biographical Directories &amp; Histories''], Glasgow entries, source code GF: George Fisher &amp; Co., ''Biographical Directory of the Voters and Tax-Payers of Kendall County, Illinois'' (Chicago, 1876). Index locators retained from the earlier research; the biographies themselves have not been examined.</ref>

Copy identifiers include '''yale.39002070892337''', '''uiuo.ark:/13960/t4fn12z83''' and '''nnc1.cu01651218'''; the Illinois copy is associated with Internet Archive identifier '''biographicaldire00fish'''.<ref name="KendallCatalogue">HathiTrust catalogue, [https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/009833464 record 009833464] and [https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008718397.marc MARC record 008718397], ''Biographical Directory of the Voters and Tax-Payers of Kendall County, Illinois'' (1876).</ref>

The actual entries on pages 95, 97 and 102 remain unread. The Sr./Jr. labels and the shared page do not establish a father-son relationship or identify the Irish birthplace. No biography text or migration date has been inferred from the index.

=== Possible later identification of the two-year-old Robert ===

A potentially corresponding '''Robert Glasgow (1849-1919)''' appears in the FamilySearch tree as husband of '''Margaret Jane Akin/Aiken''', with a marriage dated '''9 June 1870 in Will County, Illinois'''. Her source list includes an Illinois county-marriage entry transcribed as '''Margret Aron'''. The approximate age and the Aiken name in the 1876 directory make this a useful identification to test, not an established connection.<ref name="RobertJuniorTree">[https://ancestors.familysearch.org/en/9KMH-FTW/margaret-jane-akin-1847-1910 FamilySearch Family Tree, Margaret Jane Akin (1847-1910), 9KMH-FTW], spouse Robert Glasgow (1849-1919), 9KMH-FT7; source list includes ''Margret Aron, Illinois, County Marriages, 1810-1940''. Tree summary and source locator, not an inspected original marriage record.</ref>

=== Unassigned probate reference ===

The imported profile mentioned an '''1851 County Antrim probate-index occurrence''' for Robert Glasgow without an individual archive reference, residence, role or transcription. It is not usable evidence for this man. The proposed father's known will was written in 1851 but proved in 1854; that does not establish that the unidentified index occurrence refers to the same document. A deceased testator whose probate was granted in 1851 could not also be the man recorded alive in Illinois in 1880.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search], generic locator retained from the imported profile; the purported individual 1851 entry has not been verified.</ref>

=== 1880 Illinois Census === 

Robert is indexed as “Robert Glasgo,” Plainfield, Will County, Illinois; image 815/906, ED 210, sheet 405D. The record gives age 68, married, head of household, born Ireland, with both parents born Ireland, spouse Margaret Glasgo<ref>https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYYB-3RN?view=index&personArk=%2Fark%3A%2F61903%2F1%3A1%3AMX2S-9NW&action=view&lang=en</ref>
